turn_text: Consumer brief prices were up four and a half percent last month. Ranchers, Calcalf producers, as I understand, they're not seeing any additional dollars at this point. What have we learned about the imbalance and what are your concerns or suggestions here?

We need more competition in the marketplace. Capitalism doesn't work when you have consolidation, and that's what we have in the meat industry right now. And everybody needs to make a profit. And what we're seeing right now is the Packers are making a real profit. Our cap folks are going broke, and our small and medium sized feeders are going broke. I talked about the food chain a second ago as it applied to the drought. If we don't do something at the federal level, this is going to be bad, really bad, for our food chain. These folks go broke. It's going to change the look of this country, and it's going to change food security in this country forever. So what needs to happen? We need to address the issue of consolidation. This is not a new problem. It's been around, you know, for 30, 40, 50 years. And right now, we've got four companies that control 80% of the meat in this country. That's not competition. That's the four people going on in a golf course and figuring out what they're going to pay and what they're going to charge, the consumer. And so we've got a bill that was passed over a hundred years ago called the Packers and Stockyard Act. It is never, I shouldn't say never, but let's put it this way. It could have more teeth in it. And so Senator Grassley There's been around here for a long time and myself have dropped in a bill to put a special investigator in the Department of Agriculture that have investigatory powers and subpoena powers to be able to put some teeth into the Packers and Stockyards Act so that if there is collusion and there is price fixing, that these folks can be held accountable.
